'''''Convolvulus althaeoides''''' is a species of [[morning glory]] known by the common names '''mallow bindweed'''<ref>{{PLANTS|id=COAL4|taxon=Convolvulus althaeoides|accessdate=17 January 2016}}</ref> and '''mallow-leaved bindweed'''.<ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007 |accessdate=2014-10-17 }}</ref> This flowering plant is native to the [[Mediterranean Basin]], but it is occasionally seen in other areas of similar climate, such as [[California]] in the United States, where it has been [[Introduced species|introduced]]. This is a climbing perennial plant with solitary flowers on long [[Peduncle (botany)|peduncles]]. The flower is a funnel-shaped pink bloom three or four centimeters wide. The leaves are deeply divided into narrow, fingerlike lobes.
